_note: Pre-sort of the 1960–1969 candidates, written by AI on 2026-11-21 from each item's Wikidata entry and Wikipedia lead. keep = an event, with suggested edits; hold = needs a person's judgement; reject = not an event, a duplicate, outside Kenya or the decade, or contradicted by its source. Under the trust-Wikidata rule, kept Wikidata items are approved with Wikidata's date; everything else waits for a person. approve = approved by AI at the owner's request on 2026-11-21: the 21 hand-written 1963 events, each checked against its article's text when written, and three Wikipedia events whose source states the date.

decisions.title: KANU is formed
decisions.summary: James Gichuru re-establishes the banned Kenya African Union, and on 14 May it becomes the Kenya African National Union after merging with Tom Mboya's Kenya Independence Movement. KANU will rule Kenya for nearly 40 years.

decisions.title: KADU is formed
decisions.summary: Leading politicians who refuse to join Kenyatta's KANU form the Kenya African Democratic Union, led by Ronald Ngala. It brings together smaller parties, including Moi's Kalenjin Political Alliance and Masinde Muliro's Baluhya Political Union.

decisions.title: First Lancaster House conference
decisions.summary: Kenya's constitutional future is negotiated in London under Colonial Secretary Iain Macleod. There is no agreement, and Macleod issues an interim constitution.
decisions.note: The article covers all three conferences; this card is the January 1960 one.

decisions.title: The Kennedy Airlift gets its name
decisions.summary: Senator John F. Kennedy arranges a $100,000 donation to fly the autumn 1960 group of East African students to colleges in North America. The programme, started by Tom Mboya, brought hundreds of students between 1959 and 1963.
decisions.note: Dated to September 1960, when the article says the programme got its nickname.

decisions.title: KANU wins the 1961 election
decisions.summary: General elections are held in February 1961. KANU wins 19 of the 53 elected seats.

decisions.title: Maasai Mara game reserve
decisions.summary: The Maasai Mara national game reserve in Narok County is established. It borders Tanzania's Serengeti and hosts the great wildebeest migration.

decisions.title: Legio Maria church founded
decisions.summary: Legio Maria, an African initiated church among the Luo of western Kenya, breaks away from the Catholic lay movement it grew out of. Its followers believe Simeo Ondetto to be the returned Son of God.

decisions.title: Strathmore founded in Nairobi
decisions.summary: Strathmore, now a chartered university in Nairobi, is founded.

decisions.title: Kenya Union of Journalists founded
decisions.summary: The union that represents Kenya's media workers is founded as the Kenya Colony branch of the National Union of Journalists.

decisions.title: The coat of arms
decisions.summary: Kenya's coat of arms shows two lions holding spears and a shield in the national colours, with KANU's rooster on the shield. The scroll beneath reads Harambee, "pulling together".

decisions.title: Relations with West Germany
decisions.summary: Kenya and the Federal Republic of Germany establish diplomatic relations in the year of independence.

decisions.title: Goethe-Institut opens in Kenya
decisions.summary: The German cultural institute opens its Kenyan branch.

decisions.title: Chemchemi Cultural Center opens
decisions.summary: An arts and cultural centre, Chemchemi, opens in Nairobi.

decisions.title: Plantation workers' union formed
decisions.summary: Several unions merge into the Kenya Plantation and Agricultural Workers Union, representing tea, coffee and other farm workers. Its head office is in Nakuru.

decisions.title: A foreign ministry for independent Kenya
decisions.summary: Kenya's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is established after independence to run the country's foreign relations.

decisions.title: The UN Security Council backs Kenya's membership
decisions.summary: The Security Council unanimously adopts Resolution 185, recommending that the General Assembly admit Kenya to the United Nations.

decisions.title: The Kenya Army is formed
decisions.summary: Kenya's land army is formed as British units are handed over around independence.

decisions.title: The Kenya Navy is formed
decisions.summary: Kenya's navy is formed. It is headquartered in Mombasa.

decisions.title: National Youth Service founded
decisions.summary: The National Youth Service is established to train young people in national matters.

decisions.title: The Kenya Air Force is formed
decisions.summary: Kenya's air force is established as a branch of the armed forces.

decisions.title: Kenya becomes a republic
decisions.summary: On the first anniversary of independence Kenya becomes a republic and Jomo Kenyatta becomes its first President. He holds office until his death in 1978.

decisions.title: A space centre at Malindi
decisions.summary: Italy's San Marco equatorial range is developed near Malindi with NASA. From 1967 to 1988 it launches Italian and international satellites.
decisions.note: Dated 1964 by its Wikipedia category; the article says only that it was developed in the 1960s.

decisions.title: Operation Binnacle
decisions.summary: Britain draws up a war plan to intervene militarily if there is a coup in Kenya in 1965. It is cited as evidence of Kenyatta's close ties with the United Kingdom.

decisions.title: COTU is founded
decisions.summary: The Central Organization of Trade Unions is founded as the Kenya Federation of Labour and the African Workers' Congress are dissolved. It becomes Kenya's national trade union centre.

decisions.title: Kenya National Library Service set up
decisions.summary: An Act of Parliament establishes the Kenya National Library Service to run the national library and public libraries.

decisions.title: Kenya Red Cross established
decisions.summary: Kenya's national Red Cross society is established.

decisions.title: Ahero irrigation scheme
decisions.summary: The Ahero irrigation scheme is set up.

decisions.title: The Central Bank of Kenya is founded
decisions.summary: The Central Bank of Kenya is founded after the East African Currency Board is dissolved. It becomes the country's monetary authority.

decisions.title: Jomo Kenyatta Foundation founded
decisions.summary: The Jomo Kenyatta Foundation, an educational publisher owned by the state, is founded.

decisions.title: The Kenya People's Union is formed
decisions.summary: Jaramogi Oginga Odinga leads a breakaway from KANU to form the socialist Kenya People's Union. It will be banned in 1969.

decisions.title: Meru National Park
decisions.summary: Meru National Park, east of Meru, is created. Joy and George Adamson raised Elsa the lioness of Born Free there.

decisions.title: Kenya creates its national honours
decisions.summary: The Order of the Burning Spear, the Order of the Golden Heart and the Distinguished Service Medal are established on the same day. They are awarded by the President for service to the nation.
decisions.source_name: Wikipedia: Orders, decorations, and medals of Kenya

decisions.title: The "little general election"
decisions.summary: After 29 MPs leave KANU for the Kenya People's Union, a constitutional amendment forces them to seek re-election. The KPU wins the most votes, but KANU wins more seats.

decisions.title: Lake Nakuru National Park
decisions.summary: Lake Nakuru National Park is established.

decisions.title: Ol Donyo Sabuk National Park
decisions.summary: A national park is created on Ol Donyo Sabuk mountain in Machakos.

decisions.title: Malindi Marine National Park
decisions.summary: A marine national park is created in the Indian Ocean at Malindi. It is said to be the oldest marine park in Africa.

decisions.title: Watamu Marine National Park
decisions.summary: Watamu Marine National Park is established, one of Kenya's first marine parks. Its coral gardens lie 300 metres from the shore.

decisions.title: Shimba Hills National Reserve
decisions.summary: The Shimba Hills reserve near Mombasa is created to protect coastal rainforest, woodland and grassland. Over half of Kenya's rare plants grow there.

decisions.title: Mount Elgon National Park
decisions.summary: The Kenyan side of Mount Elgon is gazetted as a national park. Uganda's side follows in 1992.

decisions.title: The Arusha Agreement
decisions.summary: Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania sign a treaty with the European Community at Arusha to improve economic relations. It enters into force in 1971.

decisions.title: USIU-Africa founded
decisions.summary: United States International University-Africa, a private university in Nairobi, is founded.

decisions.title: The Kisumu massacre
decisions.summary: The presidential guard and police shoot civilians in Kisumu. The government puts the toll at 11 dead; other sources say close to 100.

decisions.title: A one-party election
decisions.summary: In the first general election since independence, KANU is the only party, after the Kenya People's Union was banned on 30 October. Kenyatta is the sole presidential candidate and is returned without a vote.

decisions.note: Wikidata dates the Kenyan shilling to 1964, but the Central Bank that issues it was founded in 1966. Check the year before approving.

decisions.title: Lambwe Valley Game Reserve
decisions.summary: The reserve that later becomes Ruma National Park is created in the Lambwe Valley to protect Kenya's last indigenous roan antelope.
